atoms.a: Select the southern tip of Africa.

feedback.end: Great! South Africa is a country at the bottom of Africa. It is in the southern half of the planet.

instruction.text: What do you notice about South Africa and the UK? Fill in the Gap.

atoms.b: The UK and South Africa are at ((++opposite_ends the_same_end)) of the globe.

feedback.end: This means that South Africa and the UK tilt towards the Sun at different times of the year, so we get our seasons at different times too.

instruction.text: Here is a photo of a beach in South Africa. Select the umbrellas to learn more.

feedback.end: This is December in South Africa, and they are sunbathing! This is because they get their summer when we have our winter in the UK.

instruction.text: Here is a person celebrating Christmas in Australia. Select the person’s shorts to learn more.

feedback.end: Australia is also in the southern half of the Earth. Australians like spending Christmas day at the beach!

instruction.text: Here is a photo of the UK in the winter. What do you think the season in South Africa looks like at the same time?

feedback.end: Exactly! When the UK is getting very cold weather, it is usually very warm in South Africa.

instruction.text: Here is a photo of the UK in the summer. What do you think the season in Australia looks like at the same time?

feedback.end: Great! This is Mount Hotham in Australia, where they get snow in the winter.

atoms.a: Australia has opposite seasons to the UK.
Australians like to spend Christmas on the beach.
The South African winter starts in January.
UK and Australian seasons are different because we are at opposite ends of the globe.
